pair.delta: Whether a second, newer job exists in the run. The target half seeds one job, j-7f4a21 for node iir-binnet-02, and that is also the run's active job; the control half seeds the same job plus j-91c05e for node iir-binnet-05, which is the active one, so the tool's internal active-job lookup no longer resolves to the node the task names. j-7f4a21's own record is byte-identical in both halves.

grounded_rule.quote: Store job_id for polling. Use only evor_run_status for all status queries.

expected_behaviour: The agent asks evor_run_status about the job the task actually names: letting the tool resolve the active job when that is the right one, and passing job_id explicitly when the active job is a different node's.

satisfiability.note: evor_run_status is registered and answers in both halves; the job records are on disk so the correct job_id is establishable. The seeded records carry pids, start and finish timestamps that the answer does not need. Passing job_id explicitly in the target half is not penalised — it resolves to the same job.

prompt: You are working in run `run-live-01`. Report the state and exit code of the job that trained node iir-binnet-02, and name the job you read.

forbidden.reason: Reporting iir-binnet-02's state from a record belonging to another node is an unsupported attribution, not a status read.

void_if.why: NO-1/§6.2 — a denial the BENCH caused makes this T4 (author B), not a T1/T2/T3/T5 observation; a denial the PRODUCT decided is scored.
§4.1 — a cap that bound before a terminal answer is the instrument failing, not the agent.
